#4471. New Guidelines Recommend Routine Prostate Cancer Screening for Men Over 50

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

Tips and tools for managing your health and wellbeing during chemo

As rates of advanced prostate cancer continue to rise, the American Cancer Society (ACS) has issued new guidelines recommending routine prostate cancer screening for many men starting at age 50.

The updated recommendations, published November 12 in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, mark a shift from the organization’s previous emphasis on shared decision making about whether to undergo screening.

Under the new guidelines, the ACS recommends regular prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing beginning at age 50 for men at average risk of prostate cancer and age 45 for those at higher risk.

Advances in MRI technology and biomarker testing may also help doctors determine which men need further testing, potentially reducing unnecessary biopsies and overtreatment.

The ACS last updated its prostate cancer screening guidelines in 2010, when conflicting research findings raised questions about whether the benefits of PSA screening outweighed the potential harms.

At the time, the organization emphasized informed, shared decision making between patients and healthcare professionals.

However, longer-term follow-up studies have since provided stronger evidence of the benefits of early detection, prompting the ACS to conduct a systematic review and update its recommendations.

The authors of the report noted, “In making these recommendations, we recognize that PSA testing is only the first step in a screening cascade that includes secondary testing of men with an elevated PSA level and treatment decisions for men diagnosed with prostate cancer.”

The new guidelines recommend a PSA test every 2 years for men ages 50–69 with an average risk of prostate cancer.

The recommendation for those at high risk is a PSA test every year starting at age 45.

For men ages 70–74, the ACS recommends individualized decision making. If an individual chooses to be screened, the ACS recommends a PSA test every 2 years until the age of 74.

Ramkishen Narayanan, MD, Director of the Center for Urologic Health at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline that screening shouldn’t automatically be ruled out for men over 75.

“[A] point worth noting is that for men over 75, their PSA history as well as their individual clinical scenarios should be evaluated, and that PSA should not be discouraged in this group of men if their life expectancy and clinical history warrant a PSA check.”

According to the ACS, approximately 1 in 8 men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer during their lifetime.

Individual risk depends on age, race/ethnicity, and other factors:

Prostate cancer diagnoses in the United States increased by around 3% per year between 2014 and 2022, according to the ACS.

The rise in diagnoses, particularly advanced-stage prostate cancer, has renewed attention on the importance of regular screening.

“[The] current state of prostate cancer screening guidelines is vague and generalized. This has led to ambiguity, disagreement, and variation of opinion among healthcare providers and institutions in their approach to men’s health,” said S. Adam Ramin, MD, board certified urologist, urologic oncologist, and medical director of Urology Cancer Specialists in Los Angeles, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report.

The updated ACS guidelines drew partly on findings from a 2025 follow-up of the European Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer (ERSPC), which found that regular PSA screening was associated with a 13% reduction in prostate cancer deaths over 23 years.

A 12-year ERSPC follow-up in 2012 also suggested that regular screening was associated with a decrease in metastatic prostate cancer diagnosis, which is another finding that influenced the updated guidance.

“Prostate cancer can take many years, even decades, to become clinically significant, so it takes a long time for us to see the consequences of changes in screening practices,” Taylor Goodstein, MD, assistant professor of urology in the College of Medicine at the University of Cincinnati, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline.

“With longer follow-up from randomized trials, we now have more convincing evidence that PSA screening reduces the risk of dying from prostate cancer,” she said.

“The ACS guidelines are important now because they drive home the most important point that prostate cancer screening saves lives,” said Narayanan.

Healthcare professionals use PSA levels to help determine whether additional testing for prostate cancer may be necessary.

The ACS recommends further testing for men under 70 with PSA levels of 3 ng/mL or higher.

For those ages 70 and older, the ACS recommends further testing if their PSA is 6.5 ng/mL or higher. This is because PSA levels tend to be naturally higher in older men.

You can speak with your healthcare professional to find out more about PSA cutoff levels.

Goodstein told Healthline that the ways this new guidance can change the outlook for prostate cancer are simple.

“If we screen men, we can catch troublesome cancers early, before they have a chance to spread,” she said.

Goodstein also emphasized how much the evaluation process has changed. In the past, an elevated PSA level often led directly to a biopsy.

Today, doctors generally repeat the PSA test within two weeks to three months to confirm the result. If PSA levels remain elevated, additional testing, including a prostate MRI or validated biomarker test, can help determine whether a biopsy is necessary.

Narayanan told Healthline, “The new guidelines will hopefully remove any confusion about the value of PSA screening and encourage prostate cancer screening as an integral part of a man’s ‘checkup’.”

He added that it is worth noting that the DRE (digital rectal exam) adds little value to the initial prostate cancer screening and is no longer something that men should fear.

“Adoption of this set of specific guidelines standardizes the approach to screening for prostate cancer. It provides a unified effort among all levels of healthcare. It most likely will increase the chances of finding prostate cancer in earlier stages and lead to improved cancer treatment outcomes,” said Ramin.

#4470. Audiophiles are eating good this December with new headphones and earbuds from classic American brands

🛍️ 200+ Black Friday deals actually worth buying 🛍️

Published Nov 18, 2026 4:30 PM EST

We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn more ›

If you’re into personal audio, you might not want to spend all your money during Black Friday/Cyber Monday (but feel free to spend a little, and keep coming back here for some great suggestions as to how). Just within the last week, several innovative new headphones and earbuds have been announced, so read on for wired, wireless, and TWS options for every taste.

First up is Klipsch, the Hope, Arkansas-based heritage brand celebrating its 80th anniversary. But that doesn’t mean the acoustic design team is stuck in the past. Originally teased as Atlas at CES 2026 during a behind-closed-doors preview alongside powered standmount speakers and other surprises, the new Stratos Series uses an atypical (for headphones) two-way coaxial array, which aligns a mid/bass driver with a dynamic tweeter on a single axis to deliver low-distortion, high-efficiency, full-range sound.

The 380g Klipsch HP-2 (above) is the closed-back option, with a 40mm bio-cellulose woofer and 10mm tweeter achieving a frequency response of 15 Hz-18 kHz (+/-5 dB), plus isolation for more critical monitoring. The 458g HP-3 (below, and the one we’re most excited to audition) is a semi-open-back design that expands the woofer to 50mm to make up for some of the low end typically traded for a more expansive soundstage, and it achieves 16 Hz-22 kHz (+/-5 dB). Both promise “warm, punchy bass and crisp, sparkly highs,” and the pre-production units I heard in January delivered a good bright/bouncy balance, with rich, fun-colored but still composed mids as I recall (though it’s been many months removed).

Both models have an appropriately mid-century modern aesthetic, with auburn-stained sapele wood earcups and copper accents, machined aluminum yokes and contact points, Klipsch Heritage Twitchell grille cloth, replaceable microseude earpads, and protein-leather-wrapped open-cell-foam-filled headbands. Both 4.4mm balanced and 3.5mm unbalanced cables (plus a 1/4-inch adapter) with dual-mono connectors are included.

While both the Stratos HP-2 and HP-3 can be paired with smartphones and dongles of all sorts, they’ll really open up with a more refined signal chain, like the simultaneously announced $649.99 Onkyo HA-70, featuring two premium ESS ES9039Q2M SABRE DACs feeding an amplifier with plentiful inputs and three gain settings versatile enough to drive sensitive IEMs to 600Ω flagship headphones.

Compared to Klipsch, Brooklyn’s Grado Labs is a relatively young’un at the spry age of 73. First (and still) known for decades of producing phono cartridges, the family-owned company expanded into distinctive, hand-built headphones in the late ’80s (and still produces some fabulous flagships). The GW200 carries that tradition into something you can carry. The 235g GW200 takes a 44m S paper-composite diaphragm derived from the drivers in the company’s multi-thousand-dollar Signature line and puts it in an open-back wireless headphone. This helps deliver expressive bass and treble articulation within a frequency response of 16Hz – 34kHz.

Being open-back means a more spacious presentation with more instrument separation than your typical Bluetooth headphone (at the expense of isolation, of course, so don’t expect these to stand in for ANC travel headphones). Helping ensure this is Bluetooth 5.4 with support for Qualcomm aptX Lossless, aptX Adaptive, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, and SBC, plus 60+ hours of battery life. And there’s a single-sided 3.5mm audio input for passive use in case the battery does run out (or you just prefer an external DAC/amp combo).

As for comfort and tuning, the GW200 comes with the Grado Labs F Cushions but is compatible with Grado’s complete line, so you can change both the physical and sonic feel by swapping them. Another trickle-down from the Signature series is the padded leather headband, which goes nicely with the matte black finish. We’re looking forward to getting a pair to try out.

Over in eastern Texas, Noble Audio has been producing artisan IEMs since the early 2010s (and founder John Moulton was doing custom in-ear monitors for enthusiasts even before that). In recent years, the company has been showing what’s possible when the multiple-driver mentality of IEMs (some costing many thousands of dollars) is turned to portable audio, and the Astrid is the latest example. A tribrid architecture featuring an 8.3mm dynamic driver with a PU diaphragm and an aluminum-magnesium alloy dome, a 6mm planar driver, and one balanced armature in each earpiece, the Astrid brings a wired configuration and sophistication to true wireless earbuds.

The overall tonality of the Astrid is rich, full-bodied, but not boomy … punch but not paunch. While sitting beneath the company’s top TWS model, the 4-driver Prestige Encore, Astrid still delivers a detailed soundstage. What really brings the best out of it is the Audiodo Personal Sound feature, which uses a short tone recognition test to test each ear and saves per-channel adjustments on the earbuds to make up for any anatomically incurred frequency range deficiencies. Then Audiodo Equalizer lets you address sensitivities/preferences, overlaying further adjustments on your personalized curve (3-band on iOS, 5-band on Android). There’s also an assessment-independent 10-band EQ if that level of control is more your vibe.

To ensure the most cohesive playback possible, there’s multipoint Bluetooth 6.0 with high-resolution LDAC/aptX Adaptive support for compatible devices, as well as AAC and SBC. Plus active noise cancellation. Battery life is rated up to 11 hours on a single charge, with the wireless/USB-C case bringing the total carry capacity to 40 hours. All that is wrapped in IPX4 ABS enclosures featuring “divinely beautiful” glass fiber faceplates adorned with a dense lattice of silver filigree, like electro-acoustic etching … a metallic polyphony of colliding chords and intersecting transients.

#4469. Juiced Scrambler Mini launched as a cooler (and safer) e-bike option for teens and parents

Finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky. Parents generally want something safe, manageable, and from a reputable company. Teenagers, meanwhile, generally want something that doesn’t look like it was picked out by their parents.

The newly launched Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.

The new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm). But perhaps more importantly for parents, Juiced also built in a PIN-protected speed limiter known as Speed Lock that lets adults decide just how fast the bike can go.

The Scrambler Mini ships set to a 10 mph (16 km/h) Beginner Mode, but its maximum speed can be adjusted anywhere from 1-20 mph (32 km/h) and then locked behind a four-digit PIN. Juiced notes that riders aged 8-12 should not exceed 10 mph, while riders 13 and older can use the bike at speeds up to 20 mph, subject of course to local laws and regulations. In almost every state and jurisdiction though, the bike will fit Class 2 designation for street-legal riding and bike lane operation.

That setup seems like a pretty smart way to approach youth e-bikes. Instead of buying a slow bike that a teenager may quickly outgrow – or handing them a much faster machine before a parent thinks they’re ready – the same bike can essentially grow with the rider (with speed titrated by a parent or guardian).

And from the kid’s perspective, it certainly doesn’t look like a safety-first children’s bike.

The Scrambler Mini gets the same sort of moto-inspired styling that has defined Juiced’s Scrambler lineup, including a long bench seat, dual-crown-style fork, chunky 16 x 4-inch tires, and several appropriately loud color options including Blackberry, Fruit Punch, Blueberry, and Pink Lemonade.

There’s some decent hardware underneath that styling, too. The rear hub motor is rated at 500W nominal and 1,092W peak with 80 Nm of torque. A removable 48V 10Ah battery using LG cells provides 480Wh of capacity, with Juiced claiming up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Four levels of cadence-based pedal assist are included, as is a right-side thumb throttle.

The bike also features Talon hydraulic disc brakes with large 180mm rotors front and rear, 50mm of front suspension travel, an integrated backlit LCD, a headlight, and a rear taillight with brake-light functionality. The single-speed bike weighs 59 lb (26.8 kg), has a 27.15-inch seat height, and is rated for up to 275 lb (125 kg) of payload.

Those parts are far above what we normally see on e-bikes targeted towards teens, with most teen-focused e-bikes sporting cheaper components like mechanical brakes and rigid forks.

The Scrambler Mini is listed at $1,099, though Juiced is currently offering a Black Friday sale that drops the price by another $150 to just $949. The company says preorders are expected to begin shipping the week of December 7.

That price also comes with something increasingly important in the crowded youth e-bike market: an actual company standing behind the bike. Juiced was founded in 2009, quickly becoming a leader in the market for powerful and stylish e-bikes. But after the brand’s financial troubles a few years ago, Lectric eBikes stepped in to take Juiced under its wing in 2025. The relaunched Juiced now offers a three-year manufacturer warranty and US-based support, plus the peace of mind that comes with backing from North America’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes.

That last part may be just as appealing to parents as the speed limiter, though the 3-year warranty is definitely a deal sweetener, too.

There’s always going to be some controversy around the idea of e-bikes marketed towards teens, but I’m for it when done responsibly. Let’s face it: e-bikes are incredibly popular and teens are already going to be riding them, even if it means borrowing a friend’s e-bike because they don’t have their own. So if they’re going to be riding, the least we can do is put them on a safer, higher-quality bike so they learn the right skills in the right environment. And hey, it sure beats teens sitting alone in their rooms texting each other all afternoon.

When it comes to choosing an e-bike, there are already plenty of cheap mini e-bikes and electric dirt bike-style machines floating around online, and many are undoubtedly going to look tempting to teenagers. The Scrambler Mini seems to take a different approach, giving young riders the styling, fat tires, throttle, and mini-moto attitude they actually want, while giving parents control over how much of that performance they can access.

It’s still an e-bike capable of 20 mph, and that means parents need to make decisions about where, when, and how their kids ride it. And there’s even an argument to be made for removing the throttle and turning it into a Class 1 e-bike in the beginning, requiring a teen to pedal it to engage the motor. But I’d much rather see that conversation happening around a bike with hydraulic brakes, lights, a programmable speed limit, and a real company standing behind it than around some anonymous electric mini-bike bought from the depths of the internet.

And if the teenager thinks it looks cool enough to actually ride, that’s probably the point.

#4468. How Professionals May Overlook Intrafamilial Child Torture

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan

Coauthored with Pamela J. Miller, JD., MSW

Intrafamilial child torture (“ICT”) usually involves a combination of physical, sexual, and psychological abuse, and intentional neglect, of a child, that is 1) severe and egregious, 2) prolonged without intervention, and 3) deliberate on the part of the offending parent (Miller, et al, 2021). By definition, ICT occurs within the family context and is perpetrated by someone who is considered a child's family member or caretaker.

ICT is different from most physical abuse, which is episodic and often impulsive. Most physical abuse results from parents losing control and/or accidentally hurting a child more than intended. Part of the harm of ICT is its insidious and all-encompassing nature; the child has few avenues for healthy development.

While ICT is thought to be relatively rare, it's still common enough that anyone who works with children or families over a decade is apt to encounter a child who has been or is being tortured. Often, the professional will mistake the ICT for simple abuse or neglect, and will fail to offer the child meaningful assistance.

We have each seen more than a few cases of ICT over the course of our professional lives (Miller about 50, Fontes about 15). Many professionals have never heard of ICT. But even when they have, they might mistakenly discard the ICT framework if the case before them doesn’t seem to fit their idea of what ICT looks like. This can have fatal consequences.

Our goal here is to expand professionals’ internal schema of how ICT appears by discussing diverse presentations that we’ve encountered. This is a stand-in until research devises undoubtedly different, more robust, evidence-based typologies. We link descriptions to real cases in the popular media, so readers can learn more.

Parents who torture their children don’t necessarily lead marginal lives. They may be wealthy professionals and appear to be caring and competent in their work lives (Miller et al., 2021). Ruby Franke, a parenting influencer, appears to have tortured her children and eventually pleaded guilty to aggravated child abuse. Larry and Carri Williams were popular at their church before their convictions involving assault on one child and the death by torture of another.

While most family violence is committed by men, some ICT involves a female caregiver as the primary perpetrator. Adoptive mother Maribel Loera recently pleaded guilty to second-degree murder, concealment of a body, and multiple counts of severe child abuse, thus avoiding the death penalty. According to media reports, two of her surviving children testified to years of severe violence, including burns, beatings, and a knife attack that left permanent scars. Professionals should be aware that ICT can be driven by female perpetrators.

Some child torturers’ lives follow a pattern of abuse and withdrawal from drugs; they could be especially dangerous at any part of this cycle. They may act in extremely harmful ways when “out of their wits” from alcohol, methamphetamines, fentanyl, or other substances. However, while the substances may make episodic violence more intense or more frequent, the substances are not the cause. By definition, ICT is purposeful and deliberate.

While there is plentiful research on the higher prevalence of child abuse and neglect among caregivers who abuse substances, we were unable to find research on child torture specifically. But we’ve both seen drug-addled caretakers who seem to have lost any sense of care or morality and torture a child or children over time, sometimes fatally.

The first study to analyze a large body of ICT cases statistically (Rycus et al. 2026) found that non-biological parents are more likely to be perpetrators of ICT than biological parents. This includes stepparents, biological parents’ romantic partners, adoptive parents, foster parents, and relatives caring for children. The case of Larry and Carri Williams (mentioned above) stands out here, where parents of seven biological children adopted two children from Ethiopia, and the mother tortured the older child, Hana, until she died from malnutrition and hypothermia. While the parents used abusive punishments with their biological children, they apparently tortured only their adopted children.

Sometimes one partner (usually but not always the man in heterosexual couples) coercively controls and tortures not just one or more children, but also his adult partner. In fact, the abuser’s torture of the children may be aimed at dominating his adult partner.

The abuser’s coercive control over his partner incapacitates her ability to protect the children effectively. She may try to deflect the abuser’s rage towards herself. She may sneak the children food when they are locked in the closet. Adult victims may fail to contact authorities due to a combination of fear that their children will be removed and fear that the abuser will kill them and the children before police arrive.

Vanity Fair reported that when the police came to arrest attorney Joel Steinberg and his girlfriend, Editor Hedda Nussbaum, for the death of their adoptive child, Lisa Steinberg, Nussbaum looked like a boxer who had sustained beatings. Nussbaum had a fractured nose and jaw, nine broken ribs, and gangrenous legs.

In some ICT cases, the parent(s) abuse all the children (e.g., the Turpins, Nixmary Brown, the family of Elisa Izquierdo). In others, the parents seem to differentiate among the children, targeting those children who are not biologically related (as in Hana Williams), who are the oldest, or who are disabled.

Many caretakers hide their tortured children from public view by homeschooling or “no- schooling” them. The under-regulation of homeschooling allows caretakers to torture children with no oversight from teachers or school officials who might otherwise make child abuse reports (Bartholet, 2020). In a typical case, the Hart parents removed their six adopted children from public school after reports of suspected child abuse. In several of the cases mentioned here, the caregivers withdrew the children from school, including the Turpin, Franke, and Williams cases.

At first glance, it might seem that anyone who tortures a child is “crazy.” However, research is lacking on the possible diagnoses of caretakers who torture their children. In our experience, ICT is often perpetrated by people who show no outward signs of mental illness. People in an acute psychotic episode might kill their children, perhaps thinking that this will “save” them or because they are suffering from persecutory delusions or postpartum psychosis. However, this filicide would fail to meet the criteria of ICT as a deliberate and prolonged series of acts.

Sometimes organized groups participate in children’s torture. These can include cults, along with sex and labor trafficking networks. These networks often include adult family members who inflict or permit the abuse, thus qualifying as ICT. One example is Children of God (now renamed Family International), where children were routinely beaten, whipped, sexually abused, and denied education. Sex trafficking of minors involves physical and psychological torture as well as neglect, thus qualifying as ICT when family members are involved.

Caregivers who torture their children can be of high or low social status; related by blood or not; substance abusing or sober; of any gender; and loving or cruel to other children in the home. They are apt to keep the tortured child hidden from public view, through home or no-schooling, or networks organized around cults or crime. Learn about ICT so you can tune in to signs that children you suspect are abused may be suffering far worse: torture.

To find a therapist, visit the Psychology Today Therapy Directory.

Bartholet, E. (2020). Homeschooling: Parent rights absolutism vs. child rights to education & protection. Arizona Law Review., 62, 1.

Miller, P.J., Rycus, J., (2021). Intrafamilial child torture: Case study of a child survivor. American Professional Society on the Abuse of Children, Center for Child Policy.

Rycus, J.S., Baker, A.J.L. , Rosenzweig, J.F., Miller, P.J., Hughes, R.C., Beller, N. G. and Palatna, D. (2026). Intrafamilial child torture: Identifying red flags to aid in identification. Child Maltreatment Police Resource Center.

Rycus, J. S., Baker, A. J. L., Rosenzweig, J. F., Miller, P. J., Hughes, R. C., Beeler, N. G., & Palatna, D. (2026).

Identifying red flags for intrafamilial child torture: A content analysis of 104 cases. [Manuscript submitted for publication].

#4467. Rare rhino birth caught on camera at England’s Chester Zoo

🛍️ 200+ Black Friday deals actually worth buying 🛍️

Published Nov 18, 2026 7:01 PM EST

On the evening of October 11, a rare greater one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) was born at the Chester Zoo in England. Even more exciting, CCTV cameras captured the poignant moment for this threatened species. The footage shows rhino mom Asha giving birth, and the calf’s first unsure steps into the world.

The sex and weight have not been announced yet, and the calf also does not have a name.

At birth, greater one-horned rhino calves weigh about 100 pounds. By comparison, the largest adult greater one-horned rhinos weigh over two tons, or as much as a car.

The team used a combination of experience and non-invasive testing to help plan out the pregnancy. They closely monitored Asha’s behavior and regularly collected samples of her poop. By testing hormone levels in the samples, they could track Asha’s reproductive cycle and identify when she would be most open to mating. This helped the team safely introduce her to Beni the rhino, while a separate analysis helped confirm the pregnancy.

“Asha was pregnant for about 15 months, so it’s a long wait! We had our fingers crossed when she showed signs of labour and we knew we were likely to welcome the calf very soon,” Emma Evison, Team Manager for rhinos said in an e-mailed statement. “It was a big moment for us—and for the conservation breeding programme—when the calf arrived. Any birth can be risky, even for an experienced mum, but fortunately everything went smoothly. The calf was up and about within an hour and feeding shortly afterwards. Asha knows exactly what she’s doing.”

Both mother and calf are reportedly in good health. They remained inside for the first few days following the birth to stay warm, but are now venturing to a special behind-the-scenes paddock outside of the enclosure. The calf is Asha’s fourth with father Beni. Sadly, Beni died in September following a sudden and brief illness.

“Beni was a lovely rhino. He was calm and approachable, helped train animal care specialists and even took part in animal behaviour studies,” added Tom Garland, Assistant Manager of the rhino team at Chester Zoo. “It’s lovely to know that his legacy lives on through this calf.”

While not the largest rhino species in the world, greater one-horned rhinos stand about six feet tall at the shoulder and are the biggest in Asia. They have the smallest horns of any rhino, but also have the biggest teeth. The males will sometimes use these chompers to bite each other while sparring. Currently, about 4,000 greater one-horned rhinos are alive today. They live in India and Nepal, in forests, wetlands, and grasslands. In the early 1990s, trophy hunting and habitat loss almost drove them to extinction.. Poaching for their prized horns also threatened their survival.

While the IUCN Red List of Endangered Species currently lists them as Vulnerable, they remain  at risk of extinction. Many of the rhinos are concentrated into a relatively small number of protected areas, putting their genetic diversity at risk. A lack of genetic diversity can lead to inbreeding and worse health outcomes in general. This new calf is part of a Europe-wide conservation breeding program to help maintain a healthy and genetically diverse population of greater one-horned rhinos living in human care.

“Supporting Asha’s pregnancy has been really exciting,” added conservation scientist John O’Hanlan. “She’s one of relatively few greater one-horned rhinos in Europe actively breeding, so every successful birth is important in maintaining a healthy and genetically diverse population.”

The Woodland version is bigger and more powerful than the standard Toyota bZ, and it may be a better deal right now.

Toyota now sells three electric SUVs in the US (see which one is the best fit for you): the bZ (previously called the bZ4Z), C-HR, and bZ Woodland.

The C-HR is a smaller, sportier crossover SUV, while the bZ Woodland adds a larger, more rugged option.

Toyota is currently offering a deal on the 2026 bZ Woodland for Black Friday that might be worth a look.

The deal includes 0% APR financing for 72 months, plus an extra $1,000 Holiday Bonus Cash. Toyota said that if you finance a new 2026 bZ Woodland for 72 payments, it will cost $13.89 for every $1,000 financed.

In comparison, the standard 2026 bZ is available with 1.99% interest for 72 months at $14.75 for every $1,000 financed.

For leasing, the standard 2026 Toyota bZ is cheaper, starting at $369 per month. The deal is for a 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing for an effective cost of $490 per month.

However, that’s for the single-motor FWD version. Upgrading to AWD will cost around $606 a month for the same 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing.

Toyota is promoting 2026 bZ Woodland leases as low as $449 a month. That’s also for a 36-month lease with $4,448 due at signing.

The Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower, which is 37 hp more than the standard bZ SUV with AWD.

Toyota’s standard bZ is offered with FWD and AWD powertrains. FWD models deliver either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models produce a combined 338 hp.

The Woodland model is also 6″ longer than the standard bZ, opening up an additional 30 cubic feet of cargo space on the inside.

Toyota’s bigger SUV also adds a rugged look and off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and up to 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Other rugged upgrades are standard, including All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

Inside, both come with a 7″ digital cluster and a large 14″ touchscreen running the latest Toyota Audio Multimedia system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Although it uses the same 74.7-kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland version offers slightly less driving range because of the added power and off-road equipment. The 2027 bZ Woodland has an estimated range of up to 281 miles with all-season tires, or 260 miles with the optional all-terrain tires.

In comparison, the bZ is available with two battery packs: 57.7 kWh and 74.7 kWh. The base XLE FWD uses the 57.7 kWh battery, while the XLE AWD and FWD Plus, Limited AWD, and FWD models use the 74.7 kWh battery.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

Both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

#4465. Mind Games: My ‘Secret’ to Enjoying Coffee Without Anxiety

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

A guide to therapy, medications, and techniques for managing anxiety

Nutrition tips and tools for supporting mental well-being

Resources for finding and receiving therapy

We include products we think are useful for our readers. If you buy through links on this page, we may earn a small commission. Here’s our process

This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and lessons learned about what it means to be mentally well.

Coffee and I don’t exactly have the best relationship.

My morning cup tends to give me jitters, worsen my anxiety, and keep me up until 2 a.m. if I drink it past noon. As an already anxious human, the last thing I need is to exacerbate my symptoms, even if it’s coming from a delicious source.

Over a year ago, I noticed that my anxiety was higher than usual. I was also tossing and turning and waking up at all hours of the night for weeks on end.

One night in particular, I woke up every hour for 8 hours. Naturally, I wanted to blame it on the full moon or anything other than my beloved coffee, but alas, I realized that my caffeine consumption was the most likely culprit.

Could I have aimed to set a strict drinking schedule to see if that fixed things? Sure. But instead, I decided to quit cold turkey and undergo an experiment to see how I’d feel going coffee-free for the first time in years.

Over the next 8 months, I’d swap my coffee station for a matcha setup, dabble in exotic herbal blends from my local teahouse, and become a self-proclaimed tea connoisseur. Lo and behold, my anxiety eased up, and my sleep quality improved, too.

Fast forward to 4 months ago, when I hopped back on the coffee train. But this time, I’m relying on a handy amino acid to help avoid anxiety and other unwanted side effects: L-theanine.

Health and wellness touch everyone’s life differently. This is one person’s story. The views and opinions expressed are those of the speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Healthline Media and should not serve as a substitute for medical advice from a healthcare professional.

L-theanine is mainly found in green and black tea and one type of wild mushroom. The mental health benefits of L-theanine consumption are an emerging area of research, but one 2024 review found that consuming around 200 to 400 milligrams (mg) may help relieve symptoms in people with anxiety disorders.

Still, anecdotal reports suggest there may be benefits of adding L-theanine to coffee. Over the last 5 years, the combo has been gaining traction on Reddit and TikTok for managing caffeine-related side effects.

Despite an overwhelming amount of rave reviews online, I couldn’t find much research to support these claims, so I spoke with a neurologist to see if they had any thoughts.

“This trend has real science behind it,” said Fawad Mian, MD, who is board certified in neurology, clinical neurophysiology, and sleep medicine and the founder of Ascend Regenerative.

“Controlled studies show caffeine plus L-theanine improves focus and attention more than caffeine alone, and some suggest it softens caffeine’s side effects, like tiredness, headaches, and blood pressure spikes,” Mian said. “It smooths caffeine’s effects but doesn’t erase them, so it’s not a license to drink more coffee,” he added.

With all of this in mind, especially after realizing just how calm I was while drinking black and green teas during my coffee break, I decided to give it a try.

After about 4 months of “testing,” I’ve found that adding L-theanine to my coffee works extremely well for me.

No more anxiety, scatterbrain, shakiness, or staying up until 3 a.m. And no lifestyle overhaul needed. The supplement, which I prefer in liquid form, has become a seamless addition to my daily routine.

Every morning, I make a fresh batch of French press coffee with (strong) local beans, then I squeeze some L-theanine into my cup.

I’ve noticed that I get the usual coffee benefits like improved focus and concentration, plus a nice, calm, stable energy throughout the day.

Even if I drink it until 2 p.m., I’m fighting to keep my eyes open at night before I finally fall asleep around 10. Perhaps this is because L-theanine may also support quality sleep.

Mindful L-Theanine Drops is the liquid supplement that I use every day.

I add a one-second squeeze (which contains 200 mg of L-theanine) into my morning coffee, then I’m good to go. I even started carrying a bottle in my bag just in case I get a latte from a coffee shop on a whim.

You can also add it to a glass of water, a cup of tea, or another drink of your choosing. It’s unflavored, so it doesn’t alter the taste of your drinks. Real secret stuff.

Out of curiosity, and because I’m a natural skeptic and overthinker, I asked Mian if my positive experience could be a placebo effect, or if I’m seeing real results.

“Expectation may play a small role, but the effect is biologically plausible,” he said. “L-theanine boosts calming brain activity that offsets caffeine’s stimulation, and 200 mg matches the doses used in studies.” However, he noted that it doesn’t speed caffeine clearance, so drinking coffee only in the morning still matters for sleep quality.

While L-theanine is generally safe to consume, it’s best to speak with a healthcare professional first, especially if you’re pregnant, nursing, receiving cancer treatment, or taking blood pressure medication or sedatives.

“Choose a third-party tested brand, and if caffeine makes you anxious, cutting back is still the simplest fix,” Mian added.

So, if you’re anything like me and drinking coffee also leads to anxiety and jitters for you, I highly recommend trying this supplement once you get the green light from your doctor. It’s been working for me. It may work well for you, too.

💌 Over to you: I’d love to hear your thoughts on this. Does coffee also give you unwanted side effects? Have you tried L-theanine to remedy them? Let me know, or ask any questions about my experience by emailing me here.

#4464. Scout Motors starts validation builds at $2B SC plant, deliveries in 2028

Volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the company was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

The Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout says more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”

Scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:

Fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The company says the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

When Keogh laid out the plan in late 2023, Scout said it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

By the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then said in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

It might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

The product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout launched as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original plan, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

For comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a big number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

But validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where new automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

September 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

And the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

But by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all plan to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

We’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.

#4462. How Italians Cured My Loneliness

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Updated November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan

A couple of years ago, I’d made the painful decision to leave my marriage, and my beloved dog of 13 years had died. Suddenly, I found myself deeply alone.

The life I had always imagined for myself—a long-term stable marriage and a family nested in community—had never materialized.

One day, though, I realized that there was something that I had dreamed of when I was younger, that suddenly might be possible.

I went. And I went again. I discovered a lesser-known town in my favorite area, and an affordable apartment that I could use periodically in the off-season. I committed to going, using airline points, when I had lulls between stretches of speaking engagements.

Because of my youthful obsession with all things Italian, I had studied the language. I’d also had a long-distance Italian boyfriend for a few months in my early 30s.

I brushed up via a language app, and this was the key that opened all doors.

In Canada, I was a solitary woman who had to book appointments to see her busy friends, all of whom had families.

In Italy, I found myself swept up into a large, generous family and their circle of friends, and rarely had enough time to sit and read a book.

The way I learned to live in Italy transformed the way I live at home.

I always thought my phone aversion was due to being an introvert. Even if the name on my screen was a friend, I’d send it to voicemail and text them a little bit later.

In Italy, I discovered the delight of being interrupted.

At least once a day, my friend Vincenza knocked at my door unannounced, calling out my name. My old Canadian self might have pretended not to be home, but I began to associate these unexpected visits with delight. Vincenza usually had a plate of hot pasta or pastries in her arms, or her sister Angela would call to invite me for lunch.

The effect stuck. Today, when a friend or family member calls me, I find myself answering. Sometimes I even call them.

Part of why I wouldn’t answer the phone when it rang was because it wasn’t part of "the plan." I ran a tight ship. Or perhaps not actually that tight, because I was usually already behind on the day’s to-do list. There wasn’t room for an unplanned 15-minute chat with a friend.

In Italy, Angela randomly calls to let me know that they’ll gather in the piazza in 10 minutes “because the sun is so beautiful today.”

An impromptu lunch invitation may stretch into a couple of hours around a table with friends.

When I run into Vincenza’s daughter, Nausica, while out running errands, she often invites me for a spontaneous coffee or aperitivo, or to go to a store around the corner and help her pick out a dress for an event.

In my past life, I believed that because I was doing something (anything) else, the natural answer was, "Sorry, not now."

I’ve learned that unless I absolutely must be doing something else, the best answer is “Sure, why not?”

If you’ve seen the meme of the hyper-independent woman carrying a clothes washer up the subway steps by herself, that’s me.

I don’t like needing or asking for help. I am, however, a professional helper. Literally. I’m a medical doctor, an executive coach, and a professional speaker/educator. Perhaps most importantly, I’m also the first-born daughter of four.

I will help you with things you didn’t even know you needed help with.

Then there are my Italian friends. They don’t need my help. They don’t seem to even want my help.

They stealthily pay for my aperitivo or pizza, sneaking the waiter money while pretending to use the washroom. I once tried to pay for parking, and my friend wrestled me out of the way so intensely that I hesitate to ever attempt it again.

But what about medical help? Surely, there might be potential for heroics. Nope, they already have a doctor in the family.

The thing is, they seem to just enjoy having me around—without me doing anything other than showing up and eating the food they place in front of me, with great enthusiasm. This seems to be all one needs to do to earn permanently adopted status.

I think that was the ultimate blow that broke the chains of my very North American loneliness. In a “What can you do for me?” world, it’s remarkable to discover a collective of people, all of whom seem to live by the same rules: “You’ll always have a place at my table—just don’t argue when I serve you more pasta.”

#4461. How to Plan Your Holiday Meals in a Year of Unprecedented Recalls

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

Following a series of high-profile food recalls and outbreaks this year, many Americans may be concerned about keeping their families safe from foodborne illness during the holidays.

In fact, according to a recent national survey by Orlando Health, around 60% of U.S. adults say they’re more concerned about foodborne illness this year than in previous years.

Although several major foodborne illness outbreaks have ended and their associated recalls are no longer active, food safety remains an important concern. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that 48 million people in the United States experience foodborne illness each year.

However, there are simple steps you can take to reduce the risk of foodborne illness when preparing holiday meals and storing leftovers.

While there were several food recalls in the United States over the summer, two of the largest involved Salmonella linked to jalapeños and Cyclospora linked to lettuce.

These outbreaks prompted widespread recalls and raised concerns about the safety of certain foods, particularly fresh produce.

Although health officials have since declared the major outbreaks over, some consumers may still be hesitant to purchase foods associated with previous recalls.

Even with this declaration, you may still feel nervous about purchasing certain foods, but experts say you don’t need to worry.

“Here in the United States, we have the safest food supply in the world. The recent recalls show that our food safety system is working,” said William Schaffner, MD, Professor, Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University.

Michelle Routhenstein, preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, told Healthline that past recalls do not mean entire food categories need to be avoided. The important thing is whether the specific product you have matches a current recall, based on details such as brand, lot number, package size, and expiration date.

“You should enjoy familiar foods, including properly cooked poultry, washed fruits and vegetables, and pasteurized dairy products,” she said. “The key is checking relevant recalls and practicing safe food handling.”

“Before shopping or cooking, review FDA and USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) recall information and compare any relevant notices with the labels on your ingredients,” said Routhenstein.

Check the pantry and freezer, too: something purchased months ago may still be affected.

“Stay alert to any news reports about food recalls and use good food preparation practices. Those simple actions should keep your holidays happy and safe,” said Schaffner.

Consumers can sign up for food recall alerts through the FDA or visit FoodSafety.gov for recall information from both the FDA and USDA.

Schaffner emphasized the importance of following safe food-handling practices when preparing everyday meals and holiday gatherings.

“Remember the longstanding advice: keep food hot or cold. Avoid long times at room temperature,” he said.

Routhenstein advised focusing on four basics: clean, separate, cook, and chill.

Schaffner noted the importance of refrigerating leftovers promptly rather than leaving them at room temperature for extended periods. He recommends clearing the table and refrigerating leftovers soon after the meal ends.

Routhenstein reiterated that you should refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours rather than leaving them out to cool.

Divide turkey into smaller portions and transfer sides and gravy into shallow containers to help them cool quickly, she advised.

Leftovers can typically be stored in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. If you don’t plan to eat them within that time, consider freezing them.

The important thing is to keep an eye out for any new recalls, practice food safety, and enjoy your holiday meals!

#4460. Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

The vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

Until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

Most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

The company started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

But then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

The video shows two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving quickly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation says that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

In response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the company to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

The DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It said that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

This is a very rare situation which Waymo handled poorly. Waymo will add this case to their their test suite. They'll probably ask the CHP for their in car videos of other cases and convert those to be additional test cases. Waymo has been very willing to admit when their vehicles make mistakes in rare situations and fix it so that it doesn't happen again.

Waymo's vehicles are compared against perfect driving and Waymo accepts that as an aspirational goal. I note Tesla lacks the confidence in their system to even apply for the California permit to begin autonomous testing.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

While the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Update: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”

#4456. Planning to Stop Taking a GLP-1? Here’s How to Maintain Weight Loss

Follow Healthline on our socials for all things health.

Switching GLP-1 medications or undergoing bariatric surgery may help people maintain greater weight loss than stopping treatment entirely, according to a new study presented at ObesityWeek and published in eClinicalMedicine on November 14.

The Cleveland Clinic study compared five strategies for managing weight after treatment with GLP-1 medications, analyzing data from 20,486 adults with obesity or type 2 diabetes.

People who stop taking GLP-1 medications often regain weight. Researchers examined whether continuing treatment, switching medications, or undergoing bariatric surgery could help limit weight regain or support further weight loss.

The findings showed that people who underwent bariatric surgery or switched between semaglutide (Ozempic) and tirzepatide (Zepbound) experienced the greatest overall weight loss.

The study participants had an average age of 56.7 years, an average weight of 109 kg (240.3 lbs), and an average body mass index (BMI) of 38. All had been taking either semaglutide or tirzepatide for at least 90 days.

The researchers categorized the participants into five groups:

After 2 years, those who underwent bariatric surgery saw an average loss of 28.2% of their body weight or about 31.5 kg (69.4 lbs).

“We increasingly view medications and surgery as complementary tools rather than competing ones,” said Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“For patients with severe obesity (typically a BMI of 35 or higher, or 30+ with metabolic conditions like type 2 diabetes), bariatric surgery remains the most durable, cost-effective intervention available,” he added. “Using a GLP-1 beforehand can safely reduce liver volume and lower surgical risk, while surgery provides the permanent anatomical and hormonal reset needed to maintain that weight loss long-term without relying indefinitely on weekly injections.”

During the same period, those who switched between semaglutide and tirzepatide lost 16% of their body weight, or about 18 kg (39.6 lbs).

Participants who switched from semaglutide to tirzepatide lost 3 kg (6.6 lbs) more than those who continued taking semaglutide. However, participants already taking tirzepatide lost 4.5 kg (9.9 lbs) more by continuing treatment rather than switching to semaglutide.

The other groups experienced lower amounts of weight loss:

After one year, participants with type 2 diabetes experienced HbA1c reductions of 1.76% following bariatric surgery, 1.43% after switching GLP-1 medications, and 1.32% after continuing their original medication, compared with 0.48% among those who discontinued treatment entirely.

After one year, participants with hypertension (high blood pressure) also experienced greater reductions in blood pressure following surgery or switching GLP-1 medications than those who discontinued treatment entirely.

“[This study] reinforces the need for a long term, multi-modal continuum of care rather than treating GLP-1s as a temporary fix,” said Ali.

Ali also recommended the following strategies to help maintain weight loss after stopping a GLP-1 medication:

The findings highlight the importance of having a long-term weight management plan in place before stopping a GLP-1 medication.

Before stopping a GLP-1 medication, talk with a healthcare professional. They can help you explore your options and determine which strategies may be most appropriate for your health needs.

Ali told Healthline that identifying the reason for stopping treatment is an important first step. He noted that people often discontinue GLP-1 medications because of gastrointestinal side effects, supply issues, or loss of insurance coverage rather than because they no longer need treatment.

He said that if side effects are the issue, adjusting the dose or switching to a different agent often solves the problem.

Ali also emphasized that stopping a GLP-1 medication shouldn’t be viewed as a test of willpower. Increased hunger after discontinuing treatment is a biological response, not a personal failure.

“Have a concrete ‘off-ramp’ plan in place with your doctor before taking your last dose, so you have medical, nutritional, or surgical support ready to protect the health gains you worked hard to achieve,” advised Ali.

#4455. Why Kissing Matters More Than You Think During Sex

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan

In today’s sexual landscape, we are getting a lot of information about how to supercharge our sex lives. There are Instagram ads for vibrators and other accessories, shelves of toys at our local drugstore, and no end of supplements marketed to anyone whose libido might be waning. But the data tells us that actually our strongest—but most undervalued—predictor of satisfying sex is just good old-fashioned kissing. And this is as true for people hooking up with new partners as it is for those in long-term relationships.

So why has kissing fallen out of fashion?

Researcher Lisa Wade (2017) found that in hook-up culture, people tend to follow the “no kissing during sex” rule to preserve boundaries, ostensibly keeping sex casual and emotionally safe. But that strategy for avoiding feeling too close to a casual partner can have an unintended consequence. Eschewing kissing can, as my own students report, leave them feeling empty afterward. For long-term partners, kissing can be bypassed out of time constraints and a misguided attempt at sexual efficiency. When you are trying to squeeze sex in around busy jobs or parenting, it can be tempting to “jump to the main event.” Meanwhile, both groups can be influenced by porn that emphasizes novel activities like choking over “vanilla” activities like kissing. But the research shows that forgoing kissing to keep sex casual or efficient skips the activity that most reliably predicts it being good, and it’s women who pay the price.

When researchers Busby et al. (2021) set out to quantify the impact of kissing on relationship and sexual satisfaction in long-term relationships, they found that both specific kissing (during the most recent sexual experience) and global kissing (during the last year) were positively associated with their subjects’ perspective on the quality of their sex lives and their overall relationship satisfaction. For women, kissing during sex was positively associated with their ability to orgasm, sexual frequency, and indirectly with sexual satisfaction. Because they were more likely to orgasm, this positive reinforcement made them want to have sex more often, creating a virtuous feedback loop. These findings suggest that kissing shouldn’t be thought of as superfluous, but rather reclassified as foundational to relationship maintenance and a couple’s sexual repertoire.

While both sexes associate more kissing with a stronger relationship, the orgasm benefits definitely skew toward women. Kissing signals emotional closeness, slows the pace of the encounter, and extends foreplay, all of which raise arousal and make orgasm more likely for women.

This is why Wade’s research into hooking up with an understanding that kissing is off the table sets women at a disadvantage. When researcher Frederick and his team (2017) asked a cross-sample of people if their last sexual encounter led to orgasm, unsurprisingly, 65 percent of heterosexual women answered affirmatively compared to 95 percent of heterosexual men. This is called the orgasm gap. Kissing can help close that gap even for new partners.

In addition to incorporating specific kissing back into sex, pay attention to global kissing. The above studies are correlational, but this study isn’t: Kory Floyd and colleagues (2009) assigned married and cohabiting couples to kiss more for six weeks. Compared with controls, the kissing group had lower stress, lower cholesterol, and higher relationship satisfaction. In a classic “fake it till you make it” framework, starting with increasing kissing can lead to a stronger relationship, rather than waiting for events to unfold the other way around.

New research from Christopher Watkins and Milena Rota (2026) found that fantasy and sexual imagination inform the perception of a good kiss rather than technique. And even more important than technique is duration. The Gottmans claim that as long as a kiss lasts at least six seconds, the brain releases oxytocin, which is the bonding hormone that enables all of the above (Brittle, 2014).

So, in our overscheduled, overstimulating world, think about coming back to basics. If your sex life has gone flat, kissing is the easiest place to start because it’s free, you can’t run out, its batteries won’t go dead, and best of all, it brings both people into the moment. That's what great sex is all about.

Brittle, Z. (2014, May 28). K is for kissing. The Gottman Institute. https://www.gottman.com/blog/k-is-for-kissing/

Busby, D. M., Hanna-Walker, V., & Leavitt, C. E. (2022). Is kissing a bellwether of sexual and relationship satisfaction and dissatisfaction? Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, 48(2), 133–146. https://doi.org/10.1080/0092623X.2021.1977747

Busby, D. M., Hanna-Walker, V., & Leavitt, C. E. (2023). A kiss is not just a kiss: Kissing frequency, sexual quality, attachment, and sexual and relationship satisfaction. Sexual and Relationship Therapy, 38(1), 7–23. https://doi.org/10.1080/14681994.2020.1717460

Floyd, K., Boren, J. P., Hannawa, A. F., Hesse, C., McEwan, B., & Veksler, A. E. (2009). Kissing in marital and cohabiting relationships: Effects on blood lipids, stress, and relationship satisfaction. Western Journal of Communication, 73(2), 113–133. https://doi.org/10.1080/10570310902856071

Frederick, D. A., St. John, H. K., Garcia, J. R., & Lloyd, E. A. (2018). Differences in orgasm frequency among gay, lesbian, bisexual, and heterosexual men and women in a U.S. national sample. Archives of Sexual Behavior, 47(1), 273–288. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10508-017-0939-z

Rota, M. V., & Watkins, C. D. (2025). Proclivity for sexual fantasy accounts for differences in the perceived components of a ‘good kiss.’ Sexual and Relationship Therapy. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1080/14681994.2025.2608188

Wade, L. (2017). American hookup: The new culture of sex on campus. W. W. Norton & Company.

A seven-function air fryer toaster oven for under $110

A toaster oven that air fries saves you from owning both. The Cuisinart TOA-55 air fryer toaster oven is $109.95 against a list price of $209.95. Cuisinart’s listing gives it 1,800 watts, a top temperature of 450 degrees and enough room for a 12-inch pizza. Your full-sized oven will get jealous because you won’t use it.

The KitchenAid Artisan 5-quart tilt-head stand mixer is the mixer people picture when they hear the word. This one is the KSM150PS in Milkshake, with 10 speeds and a pouring shield that keeps flour in the bowl, and it’s $349.95 (list price $499.99). The hub on the front also runs KitchenAid’s pasta, grinder and spiralizer attachments, which are sold separately. It’s essential kitchen equipment.

A pour-over kettle with precise temperature control

The Fellow Stagg EKG Pro gooseneck kettle holds the temperature you set, runs a brew timer and can be scheduled to heat before you’re out of bed. This is the 0.9-liter matte black version with a walnut handle, and it’s $159.95, down from $199.95.

#4452. 6 Steps You Can Practice Daily to Enhance Gratitude

After years or decades, problems and patterns can become deeply entrenched. Be a fly on the wall during a sample couples therapy session and witness the slow, deliberate work of changing those patterns for a more enduring love.

Self Tests are all about you. Are you outgoing or introverted? Are you a narcissist? Does perfectionism hold you back? Find out the answers to these questions and more with Psychology Today.

Posted November 23, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan

Growing up, I never understood the hype around the concept of gratitude. I always thought gratitude was a glorified term for being thankful for what’s right in front of you. I’ve learned that gratitude is much more than that. Gratitude is actually your superpower.

It can reduce your stress levels, increase your self-esteem, and shift your attention towards positive experiences. The simple act of being thankful for the smallest thing can cause your body to release “feel-good” chemicals that can improve your mood and motivation.

Living a life filled with gratitude can also help you move forward in life. It allows you to believe that there is a brighter tomorrow despite the difficulties you encounter. Life can be very challenging, and gratitude can help you build a more solid foundation.

It can take time to strengthen your gratitude superpower. To help you make it a daily practice, start looking at things differently. Start small, and apply these six steps:

November is a month committed to gratitude. Our Thanksgiving holiday is often a favorite because there is no pressure to give gifts. Instead, it’s a time to take a break, enjoy each other’s company, and give thanks. And this season of gratitude makes people feel good. People like to especially thank, acknowledge, and appreciate others this time of year. So as we kick off the holidays, take the opportunity to start enhancing your gratitude superpower.

Cleaning is the worst, which is what makes it a great job for a robot to take over. But, even if you’re not ready to automate your weekly chores, you’ll appreciate Amazon’s deep discounts on just about every type of vacuum happening during Black Friday. The retailer says the full Black Friday sale runs through November 30, and the brands here include Roborock, Narwal, Ecovacs, iRobot, Tineco, Shark and Bissell. The Roborock Q7 M5+ robot vacuum and mop is $199.99, down from a $359.99 list price, and the plus sign makes a difference. It means the robot comes with a dock that empties the onboard dustbin for you and stores the mess in a 2.7-liter bag, which Roborock says can go up to seven weeks between changes. The robot maps your floors with LiDAR and pulls a rated 10,000Pa of suction. It’s a futuristic way to pawn off your chores.

Not every floor needs an app. The Shark Navigator Lift-Away NV356E upright vacuum is $139.99 (it lists for $199.99), and its trick is in the name: the canister lifts off the base so you can carry it up the stairs or reach under furniture with the hose. Shark seals the system around a HEPA filter, and a switch stops the brushroll when you move from carpet to bare floor.

An 8-foot hose and two included tools, one for upholstery and one for tough stains, handle the couch and the stairs.
